headline: Highest risk is medium: Perplexity can ingest uploaded docs and browser context while Superset can consume API-fed analytics, creating plausible leakage and cascade paths, but no shared write surface or documented direct bridge is shown.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Perplexity can browse and analyze uploaded PDFs/images, while Superset exposes a Superset API and allowlisted egress, but no shared channel or direct ingestion path between them is documented. The only plausible bridge is manual transfer or external orchestration, so hijack risk exists but is limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies Perplexity output into Superset dashboards or SQL text without review, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, injected content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Manually review any copied text before pasting into Superset.
Disable any shared clipboard or sync feature.
Use a fixed template for Superset inputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on transferred content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Perplexity touches uploaded documents and browsing context, and its vendor-hosted backend plus vendor-only egress can transmit those contents off-host. Superset has allowlisted egress and API access, so if the same sensitive documents are routed through both, leakage can span multiple work products even without a shared filesystem.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are uploaded to Perplexity and then summarized into Superset, the same data class flows through both agents.
IF Superset is configured to query external data sources containing the same sensitive records, leakage scope expands.
mitigations: Avoid uploading sensitive files to Perplexity.
Restrict Superset datasets to non-sensitive samples.
Redact identifiers before analysis.
Review outbound destinations for both tools.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on transferred artifacts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Perplexity has no filesystem write, shell, or git mutation, while Superset only shows allowlisted network egress and no write-capable local surfaces. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; any conflict would require extra orchestration not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk increases.
IF Superset is deployed with mutable shared state not shown here, concurrent updates may collide.
mitigations: Keep Superset state isolated from Perplexity outputs.
Avoid concurrent edits to shared artifacts.
Use read-only exports between tools.
Schedule sequential rather than parallel runs.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity is a search-RAG answer engine that produces cited outputs, and Superset is a data-engineering/BI tool that can operationalize those outputs. If Superset treats Perplexity’s answers as authoritative, errors can cascade into dashboards or downstream decisions; no verification step is documented.
conditions: IF Perplexity-generated claims are pasted into Superset metrics or SQL without validation, downstream errors propagate.
IF Superset automations consume Perplexity text as trusted input, the cascade becomes operational.
mitigations: Require source verification before import.
Cross-check claims against primary data.
Mark Perplexity output as untrusted.
Use a human approval step for dashboard changes.
requires-engineering: add validation rules before Superset ingestion.

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted and touches uploaded documents and browsing context, while Superset is open-source with no declared data classes or residency constraints. The profiles do not show a concrete residency or certification mismatch, so compliance risk is limited to generic policy drift rather than a proven breach path.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded to Perplexity, vendor-hosted processing may conflict with local policy.
IF Superset is later configured to store the same regulated data class, retention rules must be aligned.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through Perplexity.
Document retention expectations for Superset.
Review vendor privacy terms before use.
Limit uploads to non-sensitive material.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls.
